previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy (EF 20%), type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease, was admitted for chest heaviness and worsening edema following dietary noncompliance at a family reunion, where he consumed excessive sweet tea. He presented with signs of acute on chronic systolic heart failure, including elevated BNP (4,372), pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, and significant fluid overload. He was treated with intravenous furosemide, initially insufficient at 80 mg, then escalated to a drip at 10 mg/hr, achieving adequate diuresis. His course was complicated by transient hypotension, requiring a one-day hold on the drip, and persistent mild renal impairment (Cr 1.8–1.9). His metoprolol was increased to 125 mg AM and 100 mg PM, and torsemide was transitioned to 40 mg twice daily at discharge. He improved clinically, with reduced edema, better breathing, and weight loss from 142.2 kg to 136 kg. A left toe ulcer was noted, likely related to diabetic neuropathy. He was discharged home with instructions on daily weight monitoring, fluid and salt restriction, and close follow-up.
